label: pyochelin biosynthetic process
description: 'The complete eleven-object MetaCyc PWY-6408 thiotemplate pathway is represented from supplied
  salicylate and two L-cysteines through pyochelin release. The PAO1 implementation uses PchD, PchE, PchF
  and PchG; it does not include upstream PchA/PchB salicylate synthesis. The shared cysteine-adenylation
  reaction turns twice per formal product. Carrier-class coefficients count reactive sites, not whole
  polypeptides: PchE has distinct aryl and peptidyl carrier domains on one chain. The three-ATP total
  is a stoichiometric derivation, not a measured yield. Native CPD-9992 specifies the pyochelin I monoanion,
  one member of the experimentally observed interconverting I/II products. Its use preserves a source-defined
  I projection; it does not assert exclusive I production, identity with the neutral I/II class, or a
  separate experimentally resolved release stereoselectivity. Native carrier names do not specify every
  stereocenter. PchE epimerization occurs after amide formation; its coupled cyclization step retains
  that scope without adding an unsupported separate reaction. Direct 2022 PAO1 structural work observes
  a PchE homodimer and bound magnesium; functional enables edges do not assert monomer sufficiency or
  a stable PchDEFG heterotetramer. The 1999 deposited PchD/E/F sequences are from PA14 and differ from
  current PAO1; the older PAO1 PchF submission also differs at six residues. Later PAO1 source and construct
  evidence is distinguished from exact engineered-sequence identity. Current PchD and some PchE/F mechanistic
  annotations retain similarity or curator inference. PchG is an unreviewed current entry, supported separately
  by PAO1 genetics and biochemical work; free-analogue measurements are not full carrier-substrate kinetics.
  PchC editing, transport, iron loading and regulation are outside this native assembly boundary.'
